answer_1.quote: tasks aim to convert key visual information from figures into meaningful textual illustration

answer_2.quote: Four widely adopted metrics are used: (1) Pearson Correlation (PC) to measure linear agreement between automatic scores and human annotations; (2) Spearman Correlation (SC) to assess their ranking consistency; (3) Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for average prediction error; and (4) Mean Squared Error (MSE) to penalize larger deviations.

answer_3.quote: Reference-free methods typically leverage multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and employ evaluation prompts to generate scores

answer_4.quote: Each generated figure summary in F2TBenchmark is manually annotated by 8 trained human annotators across five evaluation dimensions: Faithfulness, Completeness, Conciseness, Logicality, and Analysis.
answer_4.guideline: Training: Annotators undergo the annotation session with examples and discussions to understand all five dimensions and scoring guidelines. Tool: A custom web-based annotation tool presents the figure, descriptive text, and generated summaries for dimension-by-dimension scoring. Quality Control: Each summary is annotated by at least two annotators, with disagreements resolved by a senior annotator; inconsistencies trigger re-evaluation. Scoring Aggregation: Final scores by majority voting.
